chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about ghusl for janābah, so he said:

You begin by washing your hands, then pour with your right hand onto your left, then wash your private part. Then rinse your mouth and draw water into your nose. Then wash your body from the top of your head to your feet. There is no wudu (ablution) before it nor after it. Whatever thing you have caused the water to touch, then you have cleansed it. And if a man in janābah were to immerse himself in water in a single immersion, that would suffice him, even if he did not rub his body.

key_terms.أَنْقَيْتَهُ: you have cleansed or purified it by making water reach it
key_terms.ارْتِمَاسَةً وَاحِدَةً: a single immersion in water that suffices for the ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after the state of janābah
key_terms.فَرْجَكَ: your private part, to be washed during the ghusl procedure
key_terms.كَفَّيْكَ: your two hands, which are washed at the beginning of the ghusl
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution), which this hadith says is not required before or after this ghusl

ai.seo_question: How should ghusl al-janābah be performed according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the method of ghusl for janābah, outlining the order of washing and clarifying that a separate wudu (ablution) is not required before or after it. It also states that a single full immersion in water suffices for ghusl, even without rubbing the body.
